problem: The sentence 'The deflection formula treats the stack as one beam with second moment n b t³/12' contradicts the formula it is supposed to explain. A cantilever of constant I = nbt³/12 carrying W at the eye deflects 4WL³/(Enbt³), not 6WL³/(Enbt³). The factor 6 comes from a beam of uniform strength, where the number of leaves (and hence I) grows in proportion to the bending moment from the eye to the centre. A student who checks the factor with I = nbt³/12 will find a factor 4 and lose confidence in the formula.
fix: Replace with: 'The factor 6 comes from the uniform-strength assumption. The number of leaves, and so the second moment of area, grows from zero at the eye to nbt³/12 at the centre, roughly in step with the bending moment. Integrating the curvature over that varying second moment gives δ = 6WL³/(Enbt³). A stack of constant second moment nbt³/12 would give only 4WL³/(Enbt³).' The formula itself (6WL³/(Enbt³)) stays as printed.

where: Section 1, sentence 'They are placed symmetrically on both sides of the master leaf'
problem: Graduated leaves are not stacked on both sides of the master leaf. The master leaf is the top (or bottom) leaf of the stack, and all graduated leaves lie on one side of it. What is symmetric is the arrangement along the length about the centre bolt, with equal lengths on each side. The sentence also contradicts the lead ('sit above or below it') and the figure, which shows all graduated leaves below the master leaf.
fix: Replace with: 'The master leaf forms the top (or bottom) face of the stack and the graduated leaves lie on one side of it, usually below. The stack is symmetric about the centre bolt along its length, with equal leaf lengths on each side of the centre.'

problem: 'The residual stress opposes working stress, so the master leaf sees a smaller stress range' is loose. Residual stress does not change the stress range for a given load cycle; it shifts the mean stress. What nipping reduces is the peak (maximum) stress in the master leaf under load.
fix: Write: 'The residual stress opposes the working stress, so the peak stress in the master leaf under load is lower. The stress range for a given load cycle is unchanged; the mean stress shifts.'

problem: The note reads 'master, b = 75' with no unit, while every other number in the chapter carries one.
fix: Change the note to 'master, b = 75 mm' (and, if space allows, 't = 8 mm' for leaf 2 is already correct).
